name: Warp-level Culling
definition: A pre-computation optimization that rejects splats with no geometric overlap to a pixel's sub-tile before performing expensive alpha evaluation, reducing memory fetches and compute load while maintaining bit-identical output.
summary: Warp-level Culling is a pre-computation optimization that uses a cheap boolean bounding box check to reject non-overlapping splats before expensive alpha evaluation, reducing memory traffic and compute load.
